brief: PEHRA EP01 15s preview: 1080x1920, 30fps, 450 frames, zero still-image plates, Urdu voice-00 narration, dark cinema masked look; no full-film authorization, no publishing

history.note: Existing user-authorized scope; no creative or reviewer approval implied

research.question: What does a 15s dark-cinema cut of PEHRA have to achieve, and what do competing accounts measurably do differently?
research.decision: Keep the reveal verbal: hold speech dominant over music, spend picture budget on the final 3 seconds, and differentiate from the one measurable competitor (TikTok: 0.000 speech / 0.908 music) by being voice-led at 1080x1920 for 15.000s.

sources.finding: AST AudioSet classifier over the real 15s soundtrack: speech 0.528-0.746 across all five windows, music 0.020-0.184. Voice is load-bearing.
faster-whisper small, Urdu p=1.0, 4 segments, no_speech_prob 0.005. Structure is a planted line resolved at the end.
Real 2,004,627-byte TikTok download, 720x1280 HEVC, 10.495s: speech 0.000, music 0.908. Music-led competitor, no narration.
YouTube and Instagram extraction refused for all 6 yt-dlp player clients (bot-check). No claim made about them.

research.question: Which single concept earns the 15 seconds, and why does it beat the obvious montage version?
research.decision: Hold the masked figure still at the end and let the narration carry the reveal, because the measured audio profile of this cut is speech-dominant (0.528-0.746) while the only measurable competitor is music-led (0.908 music, 0.000 speech).

sources.finding: Speech dominates all five windows of the delivered cut; music stays 0.020-0.184, so a music-drop reveal would fight the mechanism.
Measured competitor is music-led (0.908) with zero speech; copying it would discard our differentiator.
Upstream decision: the reveal must be verbal, so the concept must be built around a held consequence shot.

research.question: What beat structure and exact Urdu narration make the reveal land inside 15.000 seconds?
research.decision: Four acts at 2.4/5.2/6.9/8.3/9.7/15.0, with S4 re-purposed as an unlocked gate (the turn) and S6 extended to 5.3s; narration kept to 4 short Urdu lines, line 4 lengthened to cover the longer payoff.

sources.finding: Delivered narration is 4 segments spanning 0.00-14.00s with no_speech_prob 0.005 and Urdu p=1.0; it is continuous with no dead air, so it is re-timed rather than rewritten.
Existing six-shot board with frame-exact ranges 1-72, 73-156, 157-207, 208-248, 249-292, 293-450; story beats are aligned to these, not invented.
Speech dominance rises to 0.746 in 7.5-12.5s, which supports lengthening the payoff shot where the final line lands.

research.question: Can the script's six camera moves actually be rendered, and does every shot contain real motion rather than a still plate?
research.decision: Yes, and it was proven by building a real 450-frame animatic: every consecutive frame pair differs in at least 455,481 pixels. The S6 pull-out at 5.3s renders without stutter, so the story's lengthened payoff is feasible.

sources.finding: Frame-exact six-shot board (1-72, 73-156, 157-207, 208-248, 249-292, 293-450) used verbatim; the animatic reproduces those exact frame counts.
Speech dominance 0.528-0.746 measured on the delivered cut justifies the sound blueprint's rule that music never approaches voice level.
Narration split into four segments with no_speech_prob 0.005; caption words are taken from what was actually spoken, not invented.

story_design.observations: Six beats map 1:1 onto the existing frame board; S4 is re-purposed from a second threat shot to an unlocked gate, which is the turn the idea stage requires. Captions taken from the measured transcript.
story_design.rationale: The measurement says the reveal is verbal, so the beat structure must place the turn where narration can carry it (6.90-9.73s), not where action can.

edit_sound_blueprint.observations: Cut rules, six captions with safe-margin placement, full sound bed spec, and an explicit S6 silence decision. Voice stays dominant by rule: music capped at -18 LUFS under narration.
edit_sound_blueprint.rationale: The blueprint encodes the measured audio finding as a constraint instead of a preference, so a later mix cannot accidentally invert it.

research.question: Is the hardest shot renderable, and can the voice stay dominant over the music for a full 15.000s?
research.decision: Yes. The S6 pull-out renders 158 continuous frames with every one of 449 frame pairs changing (min 361138 px). The voice sits at least 10.5 dB above the music in all 15 one-second windows with zero silent gaps, measured by comparing the two known stems directly.

sources.finding: Existing asset credits for the account; used to establish that voice clips are original generated work, not third-party audio.
Speech dominance measured on the delivered cut informed the >10dB margin rule; the feasibility test then verified the rule is achievable.
S6 occupies frames 293-450 (5.27s) making it the hardest and longest shot; it was therefore the correct feasibility target.

art_direction.observations: S6 key light falls from full to 8% across the shot, subject shrinks by 1.35x scale, background held near-black with real grain.
art_direction.rationale: The payoff shot must visibly darken as the line lands, so the image itself performs the reveal alongside the voice.

integrated_motion_test.observations: Real MP4 with real voice and real music, 15.000s, 450 frames, every frame pair changes (min 361138 px), voice >= 10.5 dB over music in all 15 windows, no silent gaps.
integrated_motion_test.rationale: Motion and audio had to be proven together, not separately, because the format depends on the voice carrying a moving image.

asset_provenance.observations: Per-asset table with licence position; voice and music are original generated work; reference media explicitly excluded from production.
asset_provenance.rationale: A repo licence must never be stretched over an asset, so each item is judged alone and blocked items are named as blocked.

research.question: Does the assembled film actually meet the measured acceptance spec, and is every shot moving rather than a still plate?
research.decision: Yes, verified on the final file itself: 450 frames, 15.0s, 1080x1920, all 449/449 frame pairs change (min 1080520 px), -14.0 LUFS, peak -2.1 dBTP, clean decode.

sources.finding: All five creative gates had real evidence files before production was allowed to run; release_gate.check returned True.
Stem-level measurement showed the voice at least 10.5 dB above the music in all 15 windows, so the production mix replicated that ratio.
Previous delivered cut's measured spec (450 frames, 1080x1920, 30fps, 15.000s) was used as the target, and the new file matches it exactly.

production.attribution: Original work: procedural picture (numpy->rawvideo->x264), voice-00 narration from production/account1_ep01/vo, synthesised 55/110Hz music bed, deterministic film grain. No third-party footage, music or samples. The TikTok reference measured this session is explicitly NOT used (reuse_in_production=false), and no YouTube/Instagram media was obtained.

editing.observations: Six shots cut on the measured frame board; 449 cuts/pairs none longer than 6 frames.
editing.rationale: The board is the delivered timeline, so edit rhythm is inherited not invented.

animation.observations: 450 procedurally generated frames, every consecutive pair differs by >= 1080520 px.
animation.rationale: Motion is generated per frame, so no still plate can occur by construction, and it was re-verified on the final encode.

motion_design.observations: S1 dolly band, S2 guard drift, S3 push-in, S4 sine float, S5 breathe cycle, S6 1.35x pull-out with key fall to 8%.
motion_design.rationale: Each shot's move is distinct so the film reads as six beats rather than one long pan.

typography.observations: No burned-in captions in this render.
typography.rationale: Captions are delivered as separate editorial copy in the story document, so no type is rendered into the picture and none can obscure a subject's face.

compositing.observations: Single full-frame layer, no alpha compositing; grain added pre-encode at sigma 2.6.
compositing.rationale: A flat plate avoids matte artifacts on the near-black tones this look depends on.

sound_design.observations: Music bed fades to zero by 13.6s so the payoff is voice-only; no SFX layer in this pass.
sound_design.rationale: The measurement says the reveal is verbal, so the last 1.4s is deliberately bare.

music.observations: Synthesised 55Hz + 110Hz pair, fixed absolute level 0.045, ramped out before the final line.
music.rationale: A harmonically simple drone cannot compete with speech intelligibility at these levels.

mix.observations: Voice retimed 1.3338x into 14.81s; final master -14.0 LUFS, peak -2.1 dBTP, stereo 48kHz.
mix.rationale: Loudness was measured with ebur128 then corrected by static gain, not guessed.

finishing.observations: h264 High, yuv420p, faststart, 39412237 bytes, clean decode with -xerror.
finishing.rationale: The delivered file must decode without a single error before QC may inspect it.

checkpoint.note: 6/9 stages accepted; production render complete and technically verified
